newsitem.title: THAILAND: GOLF-THAILAND CRAZY FOR "NATIVE SON" TIGER WOODS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-THAILAND CRAZY FOR "NATIVE SON" TIGER WOODS.

text.p: Thailand is eager to claim golf sensation Tiger Woods as its own, and the red carpet will be rolled out later this week when the Thai-American golfer arrives to play in the Asian Honda Classic.
"Tiger" frenzy has reached fever pitch in Bangkok, where Woods' Thai mother has become a media celebrity and the name "Tiger" makes young women squeal excitedly.

Kultida Woods dominated a two-hour television variety show late last week talking about her son. She made headlines in most newspapers with comments that she hopes Tiger, whose father is American, will follow in his footsteps and marry a Thai woman.

Thai people, many of whom know nothing about golf, can also spout off details given by Kultida about Woods' golf successes, his nearly non-existent Thai vocabulary and his dislike for Bangkok traffic.

Reported to be receiving $500,000 for participating in the February 6-9 golf tournament -- which has a $300,000 purse -- Woods is also expected to be given honorary Thai citizenship during his brief stay in the kingdom, tournament organisers said on Monday.
Although he has visited Thailand twice before, this is the 21-year old golf star's most celebrated "homecoming."
His schedule is already tight, and organisers said on Monday they were trying to figure out how to fit in the demands by world media who want to cover Tiger's visit.

Thai government officials hope to squeeze in a celebration to grant Woods honorary citizenship. Top politicians are said to be seeking a few tips from Woods, who comes to Thailand off a second-place finish at the Pebble Beach National Pro-Am.
"It's going to be quite a week," said one of the organisers of the tour. "There's a lot of interest."
Other top pros due to play in the 144-golfer tournament, which is part of the Asian PGA tour season, include Steve Elkington, Frank Nobilo and Curtis Strange.
